customer_acme_infra: Hey team - we're seeing streamed JSON responses from the API in structured mode get cut off mid-object when routed through our gateway. Client gets a JSON parse error. Repro attached.

jason_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the last 300 bytes you received? also which endpoint / model?

customer_acme_infra: Using /v1/generate with header `Accept: application/json; profile=structured` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. Example tail we see (note missing closing brace):

```
..."tokens": 312, "summary": "analysis", "sections": [ { "title": "root", "text": "..."
```

It ends mid-array, parser throws `Unexpected end of input` in our node consumer. This only happens when we route through our gateway (Fastly + custom edge rules). Direct to redwood-hosted endpoint works fine.

kelly_sre: Thanks. Can you run `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream"` to stream raw bytes and paste full bytes around cutoff? Also any proxy timeout/keepalive settings on your gateway?

customer_acme_infra: Pasting a minimal curl we ran that reproduces against our gateway: 

```
curl -v -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Accept: application/json; profile=structured" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

Output snippet from curl (we converted non-printables):

```
...chunk-size\r\n{ "id":"r1", "tokens": 312, "summary": "analysis", "sections": [ { "title": "root", "text": "begin" } ,\r\n\r\n```

and then connection shows `Connection: close` from our gateway. The next bytes never arrive.

maria_dev: Quick hypothesis: edge is buffering and cutting stream on idle window boundaries, or injecting `Connection: close` after our keepalive window. That could split a JSON token across chunk boundaries and server closes before final chunk. Does redwood send heartbeats/keepalives on structured streams?

dev-bot: SYSTEM: Redwood streaming runtime sends `\n` heartbeat frames every 15s by default for active streams; structured mode emits complete JSON objects when ready but relies on TCP-level keepalive for long tails.

kelly_sre: That matches. Customer description suggests gateway closed the TCP connection between two SSE chunks and the object was in-flight. Two action items: 1) customer—try disabling proxy idle timeout or increase keepalive probe, or configure proxy to forward server-sent keepalives (no buffer/flush). 2) we'll add extra per-stream heartbeats to make the window more tolerant.

jason_support: We should also collect traces. customer, could you enable `X-Request-ID` echo on your gateway and share the gateway logs for the failing request id? If you have a pcap around the time we can confirm FIN/RST.

customer_acme_infra: Got an id: rq-20260215-0432. Gateway logs show `upstream closed connection after 31s of inactivity` and Fastly edge had `backend_conn_close`. pcap shows a FIN right after a `\r\n\r\n` pair (likely chunk boundary).

maria_dev: Interesting — chunk boundary + FIN race. Possible server kept the socket open expecting more bytes but gateway considered stream idle and closed. Two mitigations we can try server-side quickly: a) send periodic zero-length padded keepalive frames (already doing heartbeats but might be too sparse), b) ensure final chunk is flushed atomically when object completes. We'll roll a quick patch to bump heartbeat frequency for structured streams sent via shared routing.

kelly_sre: For short-term workaround, customer can set a `Connection: keep-alive` and configure gateway idle to >60s or disable `proxy_buffering`/`response_buffering` depending on vendor. Also if you can route to our regional edge (no Fastly hop) does the problem go away?

customer_acme_infra: Routing direct to redwood edge removed the issue. We'll try increasing keepalive. Appreciate the quick triage.

jason_support: Logging follow-up: we'll create an internal ticket to add a retry-on-incomplete-structured-object counter and attach request id. Maria/Kelly can you link SRE ticket and planned heartbeat tweak?

maria_dev: Creating ticket INF-2026-314 with logs and proposed heartbeat bump from 15s -> 5s for structured streams behind shared routers. I'll add unit/regression test using a proxy that forces FIN at chunk boundaries.

dev-bot: TICKET CREATED: INF-2026-314. OWNER: maria_dev. PRIORITY: P2.

jason_support: Thanks — customer, if you still see issues after changing keepalive let us know and we'll run a capture with you. :thumbsup:

customer_acme_infra: Will do, thanks everyone!
